title: Scaling AI Agents Without Breaking Reliability — Preeti Somal, Temporal
talk_summary: A Temporal engineer argues that agentic AI apps are complex distributed systems whose core is a long-running, stateful workflow, and that durable-execution platforms should absorb retries, state, and failure handling so developers only write business logic.

takeaways.technique: Durable workflow execution with persisted history
takeaways.what_they_do: Wrap the agent loop in a workflow whose full execution history (call stack, retries, failures, signals) is persisted by the platform, so a crashed or long run resumes from recorded state instead of restarting.
takeaways.evidence_quote: We also store all of the workflow history uh so that you can go in and you can look at the visibility of what is happening

takeaways.technique: Retries as platform plumbing, not agent code
takeaways.what_they_do: Move retry/backoff/error-handling out of the agent's prompt and code into the execution layer, so the model never spends tokens or turns deciding to retry a failed tool call.
takeaways.evidence_quote: nowhere in there will there be statements like if something fails you know keep retrying it. All of those pieces are handled by temporal.

takeaways.technique: Signals and queries for human/agent input
takeaways.what_they_do: Model external input (approvals, new instructions) as signals delivered into a running workflow, and expose current state via queries, rather than polling or restarting.
takeaways.evidence_quote: interactions are managed through temporal signals and queries. Um, and they're stored in the workflow history.

takeaways.what_they_do: Keep the full run history exportable so it can be replayed/inspected in dev or for compliance, giving a clear record of how the agent navigated interactions.
takeaways.evidence_quote: customers want access to that history for compliance reasons or for the for kind of being able to go and debug in their testdev environment

takeaways.technique: Separate worker execution from orchestration state
takeaways.what_they_do: Agent code (workers) runs in the customer's environment under their own CI/CD, while execution state and retry bookkeeping live in the orchestration service.
takeaways.evidence_quote: your workflow, the code actually runs in your environment. And temporal cloud is where all of the execution state
